Removing hub C costs the most, 0.60, then D 0.46, B and E 0.43, while the pendant node G costs only 0.09." width="100%"} Laplacian centrality measures how much the overall connectivity of the network is disrupted by removing a node. The Laplacian energy of a graph is the sum of the squared eigenvalues of its Laplacian matrix, and a node's score is the energy lost when that node is removed. With $w_{uv}$ the weight between nodes $u$ and $v$ and $s(v)$ the strength of $v$ (the sum of its edge weights), the drop has a closed form: $$\Delta E(v) = s(v)^2 + \sum_{u \in N(v)} w_{uv}^2 + 2 \sum_{u \in N(v)} s(u) w_{uv}$$ On an unweighted simple graph every $w_{uv}$ is `1` and $s(v)$ is the degree, so this is $d(v)^2 + d(v) + 2 \sum_{u \in N(v)} d(u)$. Parallel edges add their weights into one link, self-loops are ignored (they don't change the Laplacian), and on a directed graph the edge directions are ignored. When normalized (the default), the drop is divided by the Laplacian energy of the whole graph, $E = \sum_v s(v)^2 + 2 \sum_{u < v} w_{uv}^2$, so a score is the fraction of the energy lost when the node goes. The scores don't sum to `1.0`, since every edge counts toward the drop at both of its ends. On an undirected graph the results match `networkx.laplacian_centrality`; NetworkX uses a different, random-walk Laplacian for directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (the default), divide each drop by the Laplacian energy of the graph. If `False`, return the raw energy drops. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (the default), uses weights when the graph is weighted. If `False`, every edge counts as `1`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, defaults to `"laplacian_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the raw dictionary. If `False`, store as node attributes and return self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to Laplacian centrality scores. Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If weights are used and an edge has a negative or infinite weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star graph, the hub contributes the most Laplacian energy: ::: {#b8b5bac7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["hub", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]) g.add_edges([("hub", "1"), ("hub", "2"), ("hub", "3"), ("hub", "4"), ("hub", "5")]) g.laplacian_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.3, 1: 1.0, 5: 0.3, 6: 0.3, 4: 0.3, 2: 0.3} ``` ::: ::: Removing the hub takes every edge with it, so its score is `1.0`: all of the energy is lost. On a weighted graph, heavy edges carry more energy. Here `B` sits between a heavy edge and a light one, and `A`, at the end of the heavy edge, outscores `C`: ::: {#95383b14 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} w = ec.Graph(directed=False, weighted=True) w.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) w.add_edge("A", "B", weight=3.0).add_edge("B", "C", weight=1.0) w.laplacian_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 0.9130434782608695, 3: 0.21739130434782608, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
